how: Written by the Research desk every Monday before the Plan run. hooks hold the seven hook types the hook tests use; formats and scenes hold what the studio can make. our_results come from Metricool and hooks.json; peer_sightings count posts by the tracked peer accounts that beat that account's own median engagement in the last 28 days. A pattern first seen on a peer starts as untested and is tried in a hook test before it joins the rotation. Peers give us patterns only: never their words, visuals or scripts. wild_cards is the bank of out-of-the-box ideas for the weekly wild card (research/experiments.json); the desk adds new ideas to it, marks the one it picks as tried, promotes winners to formats as in rotation, and retires an idea after two losses.

hooks.name: Question
hooks.what: Opens on a question the viewer answers in their head, such as whether a rule applies to them.

hooks.name: Number
hooks.what: Opens on one figure: an amount, a count of steps or a date.

hooks.name: Contrast
hooks.what: Old against new, or what founders think against what is true, such as $2,000 not $600.

hooks.name: Mistake
hooks.what: Opens on a costly mistake a founder makes and what it costs.

hooks.name: Myth
hooks.what: Opens on a belief founders hold that an Approved claim shows is wrong.

hooks.name: Deadline
hooks.what: Opens on a date that is coming and who it applies to.

hooks.name: Call out
hooks.what: Names the viewer directly, such as "If you pay contractors..." or "Own a US LLC from abroad?".

wild_cards.what: A real task done against a visible timer, such as reconciling a month of a sample company's books in 60 seconds, every click shown
A cartoon cast member hands over a shoebox of receipts and the cast reacts as each one is sorted, comedy first, one rule at the end
Split screen: two cartoon founders take the same decision on the same day; the screen follows both for a year and shows where each lands (approved figures only)
A running meter that counts up only an approved penalty figure while the mistake plays out, stopping when the fix arrives
The IRS and state letters a founder fears, opened one by one in a calm desk scene, each answered with the step that closes it (approved claims only)
This or that with the viewer's thumb: two documents, the viewer guesses which one an investor would flag, then the answer
A single unbroken camera move over the desk for the whole video, no cuts, every object part of one story
A 7 second loop with no voice and big captions, built to be watched three times
A founder's real question from our comments or DMs (asked publicly, name left out) answered as the whole video
A countdown to an approved deadline that shows what happens on each remaining day, ending on the date
A famous company's own published numbers pulled apart on the desk, the Research desk's case rules applying (Talha's ✅ first)
What a month end close looks like from our side, shown as the work scenes in fast motion, ending on the finished statements
